findings.title: import() invoked eagerly at module load defeats lazy loading
findings.body: The object literal calls `import("./applecalendar")` etc. immediately when `packages/app-store/index.ts` is evaluated, so every app module is still loaded (and its side effects run) on first access to the app store. The only change versus static imports is that consumers must now `await`; there is no code-splitting or startup-time benefit. To actually defer loading, the values must be thunks (`applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`) and call sites must invoke them. Additionally, if any of these module evaluations rejects, the stored promise has no attached handler at creation time, producing an unhandled promise rejection that can crash the Node process even if no code ever reads that app.

findings.title: getCalendarCredentials now returns a Promise in `calendar`, breaking other consumers
findings.body: `getCalendar` is now async, so `getCalendarCredentials()` returns items whose `calendar` field is a `Promise<Calendar | null>` instead of `Calendar | null`. Only `getConnectedCalendars` in this file was updated to `await item.calendar`. Any other caller of `getCalendarCredentials` that uses `.calendar` directly (e.g. truthiness checks or method calls) will now silently treat a promise as a calendar object, and a rejected promise that is never awaited becomes an unhandled rejection. All consumers of this return shape need auditing/updating.

findings.title: async callback in forEach: deletions not awaited and errors escape try/catch
findings.body: Changing the `forEach` callback to `async` means the loop returns immediately; the calendar/video deletions are fire-and-forget. The surrounding `try/catch` can no longer catch failures (rejections happen after the catch block has been left), so errors become unhandled promise rejections instead of being logged, and the function proceeds to send the reschedule email (and returns) before the external events are actually deleted. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))` instead.

findings.title: async callback in forEach: deletions not awaited and errors escape try/catch
findings.body: The `forEach(async (bookingRef) => ...)` callback returns a promise that nobody awaits, so the external calendar/video deletions run detached. The enclosing `try/catch` no longer captures their failures (they surface as unhandled rejections), and the email is sent and the function returns before deletion completes. Replace with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))`.

findings.title: requestReschedule deletions are fire-and-forget after making callback async
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar(...) ... })` is not awaited, so calendar event deletion / meeting deletion now happen after the tRPC mutation has already responded. Failures become unhandled rejections with no logging, and in serverless environments the process may be frozen before the deletes complete, leaving orphaned calendar events. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))`.

findings.title: Recurring-booking calendar deletes pushed into apiDeletes after it is already awaited
findings.body: In the recurring branch the callback passed to `forEach` is `async` and awaits `getCalendar(credential)` plus `calendar?.deleteEvent(...)` before `apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent)`. Because `forEach` does not await, control returns immediately and `Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` (line 652) runs with an `apiDeletes` array that is still empty for these entries. The recurring calendar deletions are therefore neither awaited nor error-handled; with the extra `await getCalendar` introduced here the race is now guaranteed rather than incidental. Collect the promises synchronously (e.g. `for ... of` with awaited getCalendar, pushing the unawaited deleteEvent promise).

findings.title: Noisy log.info of CalendarService constructor on every calendar resolution
findings.body: `log.info("calendarApp", calendarApp.lib.CalendarService)` runs on every call to `getCalendar`, which is on the hot path for availability, booking creation and cancellation. It serializes a class constructor into logs on every request, adding noise and overhead with no diagnostic value. This looks like leftover debug output and should be removed or downgraded to debug.
